country_background: Australia is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy with its capital in Canberra.{{country_overview.demographics:9}} Governor-General Sam Mostyn represents the King, and Anthony Albanese is Prime Minister.{{country_overview.government:1}}{{country_overview.government:3}} The estimated resident population was 27,921,150 at 31 March 2026, with migration driving most of the 1.4 percent annual growth.{{country_overview.demographics:1}} The high-income economy is about US$1.80 trillion at market exchange rates (World Bank, 2025) and grew 2.1 percent in the year to June 2026.{{country_overview.economy:2}}{{country_overview.economy:3}} About 17.5 percent of residents were 65 or older at 30 June 2025 on ABS-based figures.{{country_overview.demographics:14}} The key risk is inflation and rates: consumer prices rose 4.3 percent in the year to September 2026, and the cash rate reached 4.85 percent on 4 November 2026.{{country_overview.economy:4}}{{country_overview.economy:6}}
key_takeaways: Health spending reached A$290.7 billion in 2024-25, 10.5 percent of GDP, and governments paid 70 percent.{{health_system.financing:3}}
Dementia was the leading cause of death in 2025 at 10.1 percent, and cancer caused 16.4 percent of disease burden.{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:1}}{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:2}}
Overweight and obesity affected 67 percent of adults in 2022-24, and 61 percent of people had a chronic condition.{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:3}}
National data show 126,206 employed doctors and 421,796 employed nurses and midwives in 2025.{{health_system.workforce:6}}{{health_system.workforce:7}}
health_system: Medicare covers everyone for core services, and states and territories run public hospitals with Commonwealth funding.{{health_system.public_system:1}}{{country_overview.government:4}}
The Commonwealth will give state hospitals a record A$219.6 billion (US$154 billion) from 2026-27 to 2030-31.{{health_system.public_system:4}}
GP bulk billing hit 84.1 percent in April to June 2026, up 4.9 points, toward a 90 percent 2030 target.{{health_system.public_system:8}}{{health_system.public_system:7}}
market: At 30 June 2026, 45.8 percent of people had private hospital cover and 55.5 percent had general treatment cover.{{health_system.private_system:1}}
Ramsay Health Care is the largest operator, and private hospitals handled about 40 percent of 2024-25 admissions.{{health_system.private_system:4}}{{health_system.private_system:3}}
Foreign ties are mainly research and training, such as Cleveland Clinic with Epworth.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:4}}
risks: A department review found falling private hospital profitability, with several hospitals at high risk of near-term exit.{{health_system.private_system:2}}
The cash rate rose to 4.85 percent, its fifth increase of 2026, pressuring hospital operators and insurance uptake.{{country_overview.economy:6}}
More than 12 percent of surveyed practitioners were unsure about staying or planned to leave.{{health_system.education:4}}

recent.text: Ahpra reported 999,105 registered practitioners, up 4.1 percent, with over 23,000 internationally qualified first-time registrants.{{recent_developments.0:1}}
Receivers will split Healthscope's 25 hospitals among four operators, with Calvary Health Care taking 14.{{recent_developments.1:1}}
Budget 2026-27 gave A$1.8 billion (US$1.26 billion) to make 137 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics permanent.{{recent_developments.2:2}}
